details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3762-3866 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The resolver bootstrap path hard-exits with code 2 when the in-tree resolver and both fallbacks are missing or unparseable, aborting conflict resolution outright.
  WHY: All three reviewers report that this leaves no path to invoke the resolver/codex exec when the resolver script itself is broken, so the workflow fails instead of recovering.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1069-1171 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: `post_state_comment` can fail, but `|| true` at call sites discards the error and leaves the poller operating on stale state.
  WHY: Reviewers note the V2 posting path returns non-zero on missing helpers or chunk-post failures, and swallowing that return can repeat actions or duplicate issues.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3357-3478 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: `integration_conflict_dispatch_count` is preserved across successful conflict cleanup, so the next conflict episode reuses an old backoff count.
  WHY: The backoff multiplier is derived from that counter, and reviewers note the heal/clean flow never resets it, causing a fresh conflict to inherit an inflated cooldown.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3241-3251 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The awk filter uses GNU interval quantifiers `{40}` and `{24}`, which are not portable across non-gawk awk implementations.
  WHY: Reviewers report the filter can fail to compile or behave incorrectly on non-GNU awk, silently breaking conflict-file detection outside the current Ubuntu runner setup.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1678-1699 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: `detect_stalls` compares `phase_attempts_count` to the raw global `max_recoveries` instead of the phase-specific effective cap.
  WHY: Reviewers note later stall recovery logic honors per-phase overrides, so this early skip check can cut off a phase before its intended budget.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:547-835 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: `_current_reasoning_effort` only steps down on timeout and never recovers to the initial level for later retries or episodes.
  WHY: Reviewers say a transient timeout can push subsequent attempts to lower reasoning levels, including the floor, even when the higher level might have been sufficient.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5372-5390 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The `conflict_override_count` state update silently drops jq failures, so the counter may stop advancing without any diagnostic.
  WHY: Reviewers note the `jq ... && mv ... || rm -f ... || true` pattern suppresses parse/disk/write errors, which can let the budget-neutral override cap stop working.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5972-6025 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The judge replay-count and cache-reset state updates silently drop jq failures, so replay limits and cache state can become stuck.
  WHY: Reviewers note the same `jq ... && mv ... || rm -f ... || true` pattern can leave cached judge decisions replaying indefinitely or fail to reset them.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3357, 3393 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The integration conflict cooldown uses `dispatch_count` as the backoff multiplier, so a later unrelated conflict episode inherits stale cooldown state.
  WHY: `dispatch_count` is kept as an audit trail and never reset, so a brand-new conflict can start with a much larger cooldown than intended.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3247 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The awk regex uses `{40}` and `{24}` interval expressions that are GNU awk extensions.
  WHY: On non-gawk awk implementations, the regex can fail to compile and `_list_integration_conflict_files` returns empty output, silently defeating the hot-file short-circuit.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1695-1699 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `detect_stalls` skips when `phase_attempts_count >= max_recoveries`, bypassing the later phase-specific cap logic.
  WHY: The current poll path does not pass `max_recoveries_by_phase`, so this is latent today but would fire prematurely if per-phase caps were added to stall detection.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:828-835 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `_current_reasoning_effort` only steps down on timeout and never steps back up.
  WHY: A timeout can lower later attempts to weaker reasoning levels with no recovery path, so subsequent retries may run at reduced quality.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5388-5390 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `conflict_override_count` jq write can fail silently and stop advancing the counter.
  WHY: The `jq ... && mv ... || rm -f ... || true` pattern suppresses write failures, so the per-head SHA override cap can become ineffective.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5972-5974, 6023-6025 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The judge cache replay-count and cache-reset jq writes can fail silently.
  WHY: If those updates are lost, the replay counter never reaches its cap and cached judge decisions can be replayed indefinitely.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3858-3862 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The resolver bootstrap guard exits with code 2 when no clean resolver entry-point is available, with no fallback mechanism.
  WHY: When the staged resolver script and both fallback paths are unavailable, the workflow aborts the merge-resolve step entirely.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1071-1124 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: V2 state posting returns hard errors, but all posting failures are swallowed by `|| true` at call sites.
  WHY: If V2 persistence fails, the poller continues with stale state and can re-run wave-advance or create duplicate issues.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3357-3363, 3473 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `integration_conflict_dispatch_count` is never reset after a successful conflict resolution, causing stale backoff for future conflicts.
  WHY: `mark_integration_sync_clean()` clears unresolved ticks but preserves the dispatch count, so the next conflict can start with an artificially high backoff multiplier.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:829-835 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_current_reasoning_effort` only steps down on timeout and never recovers to the initial level.
  WHY: After a timeout, subsequent attempts in the same session remain at lower reasoning levels even when the higher level might have succeeded.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3247 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The awk regex uses GNU-only `{N}` quantifier syntax.
  WHY: On awk implementations without GNU interval support, the regex may fail to compile and break conflict-path stripping in `_list_integration_conflict_files`.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5388-5390, 5972-5974, 6023-6025 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: State updates for `conflict_override_count`, judge replay count, and judge cache reset silently ignore jq failures.
  WHY: The `jq ... > "${STATE_FILE}.tmp" 2>/dev/null && mv ... || rm -f ... || true` pattern can lose state updates without any operator visibility.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1697-1698 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `detect_stalls` compares `phase_attempts_count` against the raw global `max_recoveries` instead of the phase-specific effective cap.
  WHY: If per-phase caps are configured, this early skip check can trigger before the intended per-phase budget is exhausted.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3241-3247 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The awk regex `[[:xdigit:]]{40}([[:xdigit:]]{24})?` uses interval syntax that is not portable to all awk implementations.
  WHY: If `git merge-tree` emits unexpected output, this filter can fail to compile or pass bogus text into the conflict-file list, breaking hot-file conflict detection.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1695-1696 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `phase_attempts_count` is compared to the raw `max_recoveries` instead of the phase-specific effective cap.
  WHY: When a phase has a higher configured limit, the early skip check can cut it off before that limit is reached.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1069-1171 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `post_state_comment` failures are swallowed at every call site via `|| true`.
  WHY: The V2 state-posting path can return non-zero on missing helpers or chunk-post failures, and discarding that error leaves the poller re-reading stale state.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3384-3404 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `integration_conflict_dispatch_count` is never reset after successful resolution.
  WHY: The backoff calculation reuses the stale count on the next conflict episode, so the cooldown is longer than intended.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3762-3866 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The resolver bootstrap guard hard-fails when all resolver entry points are missing or unparseable.
  WHY: With every resolver copy broken, the workflow exits 2 and never gets to run the resolver.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5372-5374, 5972-5974, 6023-6025 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `jq ... || true` state-update pattern silently ignores failures for the override counter and judge cache state.
  WHY: A jq or disk failure can leave counters unchanged, prevent caps from being enforced, and keep cached decisions from updating.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_1-fast ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3762-3866 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Triple fallback failure emits `::error::` and `exit 2`, hard-aborting the resolver step before codex exec.
  WHY: If all resolver script copies are unparseable or missing, the workflow fails without attempting resolution.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1069-1171 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: V2 pack/post failures return non-zero but callers swallow them with `|| true`, leaving stale state.
  WHY: When state is not persisted, the poller rereads prior state and can repeat actions such as wave dispatch or validation re-dispatch.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:547-560 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_current_reasoning_effort` only steps down on timeout and never steps back up after success.
  WHY: A single early timeout can force later attempts to run at lower reasoning levels, including the floor, even if the original level would have worked.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3384-3404 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `integration_conflict_dispatch_count` is used for backoff without being reset on successful resolve.
  WHY: The next conflict episode inherits the stale high count and applies an oversized cooldown.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1678-1698 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `detect_stalls` compares `phase_attempts_count` to raw `max_recoveries` instead of the phase-specific effective max.
  WHY: A phase with a higher per-phase cap can be skipped prematurely by the early check.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-
